common_name: Ispahan Damask Rose (Classic Fragrant Pink Damask)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown, own-root shrubs in late winter to early spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Ispahan is one of the longest-blooming once-flowering damask roses, holding its display for six weeks or more.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Ispahan is a classic damask rose of ancient, uncertain Persian origin, bearing loosely double, clear pink flowers with the rich, classic damask fragrance long prized in perfumery. Unlike most once-blooming old garden roses, which flower for only two or three weeks, Ispahan holds its bloom for six weeks or more in late spring into early summer, one of the longest single flushes of any once-flowering rose class. Its tall, upright, well-branched shrub tolerates lean soil and neglect far better than modern hybrid roses, and needs only routine removal of dead or crossing wood after flowering. Its long history in essential-oil rose cultivation reflects an intensely fragrant flower well suited to potpourri and rose water.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown, own-root shrubs in late winter to early spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Celsiana is a classic 18th-century damask rose noted for delicate, papery, semi-double blooms.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Celsiana, a Dutch damask rose documented since the 18th century and famously depicted in Redouté's botanical rose paintings, bears large, semi-double, silvery pale-pink flowers with a delicate, papery, crepe-like petal texture and a strong, classic damask fragrance. Its relatively loose, informal flower form and prominent golden stamens give it a softer, more naturalistic look than the densely petaled doubles typical of many old garden roses. It blooms once in a heavy late-spring to early-summer flush on a vigorous, arching shrub, and its tolerance of lean soil and minimal care make it a reliable, low-maintenance choice for an heirloom rose garden. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood right after flowering.
